beats.hook: My manager told me to follow the employee handbook — word for word, no exceptions. So I did. And it cost him forty-three thousand dollars.
beats.the_wrong: He'd been denying my overtime for months, just writing "not pre-approved" on my timesheets and pocketing the hours. When I brought it up, he slid the employee handbook across the desk and said, "Everything you need is in there."
beats.the_plan: Fine. I read every single page. And that's when I found something he clearly hadn't counted on — a clause he'd never bothered to enforce.
beats.the_execution: The handbook required management to conduct a formal written review before rejecting any timesheet. Every. Single. Time. He'd skipped that step for three years — on my timesheets, and on everyone else's. I filed a wage complaint with the state labor board. I brought the handbook. I brought my records. I brought receipts going back to 2021.
beats.the_satisfaction: The audit covered the entire department. Twelve employees. Thirty-six months of unpaid hours. He had to repay all of it — out of the department budget he controlled. His budget was frozen for the next fiscal year, and he had to explain it to his own boss in writing. Here's what I still think about — he handed me that handbook like it was a weapon against me. Did he ever actually read it himself?
beats.cta: Drop a comment — have you ever used someone's own rules against them? Because I want to hear it.
